Understanding the concept is not the same as answering the question

AP CSA MCQ questions are written to test specific misconceptions — off-by-one errors, parameter vs return confusion, scope issues. Resources that teach the concept without practicing those exact question structures leave students unprepared for how the exam is actually phrased.
Students who understand Java but miss exam questions about Java

They can write the code. They can explain how it works. But multi-step code tracing questions, constructor parameter shadowing traps, and ArrayList traversal edge cases require exam-specific practice — not just general Java fluency.
Students who practice the wrong FRQ format

FRQ 3 is ArrayList only in the 2025-2026 format. Students who practiced old-format FRQs with inheritance and super methods practiced for an exam that no longer exists. That mismatch shows up as lost points on questions they should have owned.

Inheritance, extends, and super are gone from the 2025-2026 exam. Students who spent time on those topics spent time on content that will not earn them a single point in May. Realigning mid-year is harder than starting aligned.
